title: Item ID scheme
scope: **Decided:** phase-seq (`P2-01`, children `P2-01.1`); an item that changes phase keeps its ID. Recorded in `specs.md` §2 and `config.json.id_scheme`. ✅

title: License
scope: **Decided:** MIT. LICENSE lands with P1-01. ✅

title: Package name and domain
scope: **Decided:** name `gatewright`, `gatewright.dev` registered, `bin` exposes both `gw` and `gatewright` so a PATH collision on `gw` never blocks anyone. ✅ · **Open:** the npm placeholder is NOT published (needs an npm login; registry returns 404), so the name is unclaimed. Blocks P1-20.

title: Default stages for `init`
scope: **Decided:** `templates/stages.json` ships the eight-stage default (Backlog → Specified → Building → Built → In review → Reviewed → Merged → Verified) with `auto` flags set per `design.md`. ✅

title: Read-only board delivery
scope: **Decided:** `gw open` writes a snapshot with data inlined as JSON blocks; no `file://` fetch, no File System Access API, `serve` is the only write path. Recorded in `specs.md` §7. ✅

title: Repo scaffold
scope: `package.json` with `bin`, no deps, `node --test` runs, CI on push.

title: `store.js`: load/save items, append events

title: `rules.js`: `requires` evaluation
scope: All four rule keys implemented; dep cycle detection; tests for each rule passing and failing.

title: `init`
scope: Creates `.gatewright/` from templates, writes AGENTS.md block (fenced), detects and updates CLAUDE.md, `.cursor/rules`, copilot-instructions. Idempotent. `--force` replaces the block.

title: `add`
scope: Assigns ID, validates parent, prints only the ID to stdout, appends event.

title: `claim` / `release`
scope: Sets/clears owner; refuses claim if owned by someone else without `--force`.

title: `move`
scope: Enforces next-stage-only, evaluates target `requires`, prints each failed rule; `--force` bypasses ordering but never `requires`.

title: `note`
scope: Appends to notes with timestamp line; event recorded.

title: `edit`
scope: Per `specs.md` §6.5: vocab-validated, deps re-checked for cycles, all-or-nothing, one `edit` event listing changed keys. Refuses GitHub-owned fields on a linked item with the issue URL in the message (test with a fixture item carrying `gh`, even though sync is v0.3).

title: `brief`
scope: Renders the fixed layout in `specs.md` §6.1; hard cap on lines with `(+n more)`; `--me` filters dispatched/in-flight; `--json` variant.

title: `check`
scope: Reports rule violations, bad deps, cycles, stale owners (`config.check.stale_days`); exit 1 on any.

title: Out-of-band write detection
scope: `store` writes `.gatewright/.digest` (SHA-256 of `items.jsonl` + ts) after every write; `check` compares, reports `items.jsonl modified outside gw since <ts>` once, then re-baselines. Missing digest is written silently, not reported. Tests: hand edit → reported once, clean on the second run; fresh clone with a committed digest → clean.

title: `show` / `list`
scope: Plain and `--json` output.

title: `import --format md`
scope: Imports this file's item format with stage, deps, evidence, notes, refs intact; a 100-item fixture round-trips.

title: Viewer shell: read-only board and table from injected data

title: `gw open`
scope: Injects items/events/stages/config into the pinned shell, escapes `</` inside strings, writes `.gatewright/board.html`, opens the default browser (`--no-browser` skips). Acceptance: `gw open` in a fresh repo renders the board in Chrome, Firefox and Safari with the network disabled; a title containing `</script>` does not break the page.

title: check does not validate vocab on existing items
scope: add validates phase/priority/gate/type against config.vocab, but check never re-validates, so a direct file write or a later narrowing of vocab drifts silently. The live board carries P4/P5 items with priority values outside vocab.priority and check reports it clean, which undercuts check's stated job of catching out-of-band writes. Deciding warn-vs-fail matters: making check newly fail would break existing boards mid-version.

title: gw help <command> prints only the global help
scope: gw help add and gw add --help both print the top-level command list rather than that command's own flags, so the per-command flag set is only discoverable by reading source. Every command already declares a flag spec that could back real per-command help.
